title: Capacity-tilt scenario proforma & variance notes
summary: Working proforma that maps token-price / revenue-growth scenarios to headcount phasing and margin variance. Purpose: give PLG/product and Eng leads a transparent hire trigger matrix tied to unit economics and price-sensitivity experiments. This is intentionally concise — uses simplified per-token economics + incremental fixed cost buckets to enable quick tradeoffs (fast decisions for Dedicated / Private capacity commitments).

pricing_sensitivity_notes:
- Base unit: token price = current average billable price across hosted API customers (internal baseline $0.0009 / token equivalent).
- Sensitivity buckets: -30%, -15%, 0%, +10%. For each bucket we calculate net revenue delta, assume 60% variable (gpu + cloud infra) and 40% fixed (salaries, rent).
- Key assumption: quantization/optimizations reduce cost-per-token by 10% only in Aggressive growth scenario (because we invest in optimize features).
- Quick read: every -10% in price -> ~15% reduction in gross margin; net hiring capacity drops by ~1.3 engineers per full 12-month hire-equivalent in our model.
- We include a one-time migration cost line for Private deployments (avg $250k uplift per large customer rollout) in downside scenarios.
triggers_and_decisions:
- Hiring triggers: roll forward if rolling-12mo ARR growth > 25% and gross margin > 58%.
- Hiring pause trigger: sustained 3-mo rolling ARR growth < 5% OR margin drop > 8pp -> immediate hiring freeze except for critical SRE/security roles.
- Pricing action trigger: if market reference price falls > 12% vs baseline -> evaluate tiered price floors + controlled discounts for enterprise deals.
- Capacity tilt decision: shift 20% of new infra budget to caching/Optimize if token-price falls between -10% and -20%.
- Fallback: for Price-shock scenario we prioritize: 1) hiring pause, 2) delay non-critical infra refresh, 3) conservatively reprice new bookings.
